title: The Pearl set's round two: cheap on the GPU, no dot clouds anywhere, stalks held off the rock and walls, the ram's stagger and the hull's jolt, the review's fixes
context: Owner, 2026-10-13, after playing ?creatures=pearl: "promising, but 1) there are still a mix of half-dotted and new cutis enemies. the fps gets very low. hard to tell if it's just because of Cutis, or the mix. 2) the cutis getting rammed by the tank is not a satisfying animation, we need some sense of stagger on the enemy, and bump on the tank. 3) the cutis animation clips through walls, that's not good, we need a method to have their feeling/scouting appendage be constrained by the rocks/walls ... these enemies look better, but fps wise we maybe cannot afford them as is." Headed M4 soaks (vsync off, &hold=1&sentries=6): the Pearl bodies cost ~0.04 ms each over the dot clouds, all GPU (8.8-11.7M triangles at 420-630 enemies on sector 4; the creatures' CPU 0.5-2 ms); sector 6's far side 373 records left as dot clouds by maxArc 1.2. An independent review of the branch listed five fixes (pool exhaustion, the slow's ice, per-frame garbage, a faded pearl's depth, the probe's validity). Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-pearl-enemies-design.md, "Round 2"; branch pearl-enemies, local.
outcome: PERFORMANCE (src/fx/cutis-maku/geometry.js, hard-core.js; CUTIS_LOD, PEARL_FOLLOW.lod): only the bodies that can be seen are packed (the camera's frustum with a sphere wide enough for the longest stalk, and the planet's horizon; nothing culled while the story monitor or the SOL-82 scope draws a second view); three hulls: the kit's high (13k, two passes) over 70 device px of radius and at most 12 a tier, the kit's low (2.2k) over 12 px, a new ~450-triangle one below; the soft inner core one resolution down and none at the lowest level; the pearl at two resolutions; 4x4 contact shadows. NO DOT CLOUDS (src/domain/surface-hubs.js, src/fx/creature-bodies.js): twelve projection hubs on the icosahedron, the first at the heart (every point within 0.65 rad), each record on its nearest with 0.03 rad of hysteresis, handed over at the same sphere pose (origin, anchor, hunt point, heading re-projected; the hop goes on); one swarm per tier still draws them all, each instance's hub index in iState.w and the twelve turns a uniform table (HUB_TURN); maxArc gone; a body that cannot be made is refused and its record made again as its own dot cloud. THE ROCK AND THE WALLS (src/domain/body-reach.js, swarm.js reachLimit): the free reach along a plane direction on a fixed 1.5 m grid, bisected, the cell graph walked from the record's cell (the neighbours' neighbours looked at before it stops); every seeking stalk held 0.6 radii short of the first BLOCKED cell, so its anchor and transfer are clear; a heading whose stalks are all blocked turns to the clear way that best nears its target. THE RAM (presentation only, PEARL_IMPACT): a rammed body's stalks snap back, it is knocked 1.4 radii along the heading and aside, squashed and rebounding (the deflate channel, signed) for 0.45 s before its deflate; a cored body's touch recoils it (0.8 radii back, a harder wobble, 0.5 s held, alive); the hull's jolt (src/fx/ram-jolt.js: a damped pitch and roll and a camera dip scaled by the body's size, sharper for a cored one, merged kicks and a draining load so a crowd rumbles, clamped) through five existing td-tab lines; enemy-step calls rammed/touched, the rules untouched. THE REVIEW: the slow's ice kept (the stand-in's setTint to the body's tint channel: membrane and pearl), no per-frame garbage (coreContactInto, positionInto, toPlaneInto, the seam's kept options object, lead and leash cached, a min-heap of free slots), a fading pearl drawn by a depthless twin, the probe counting only drawn bodies (alive + pending topped up, dying and pending per step, pending, refused and the last error on the card).
alternatives: one hub per region with its own set of per-tier swarms (the task's suggestion): up to 96 pools, a hull build hitch at each pool's first body and a handover that moves a body between pools; one swarm per tier with a per-instance hub turn moves nothing but plane coordinates

the hub's quaternion as a per-instance vec4 attribute: passes WebGL's sixteen vertex attributes with three's declared ones ("Too many attributes (iHub)"); the index packed in iState.w with a uniform table instead
six hubs on the octahedron: a shape pressed up to 17 % at a face centre and up to that much change at a hand-over; the icosahedron's twelve keep both under 7.5 %
hide the bodies from the bloom's weighted pass to halve their draws: their glow is part of their look (the bloom bites at 0.2); with the culling and levels the second pass costs little
the stalks clamped against the dungeon's tags along a plain greedy cell walk: it stopped on a local best now and then (1-2 of ~210 stalks read differently from the next record cell)
the tank's jolt for every ram (the dot clouds too): the owner asked for the Pearl bodies; the game without ?creatures=pearl is unchanged
evidence: headed M4 soaks through scratchpad soak.mjs (150 s, means after 20 s; index.html?skip=defence&hold=1&sentries=6&sector=N[&creatures=pearl]&fps=1): sector 4 dots 22.7 ms (25-27 ms at 410-536 enemies), 1.75M triangles; Pearl before 34.4 ms (42-49 ms at 440-495), 6.5M mean, 8.8-11.7M at the peaks; Pearl after the culling and levels 20.5 ms (20.6-21.8 ms at 422-631), 2.1M (2.0-2.7M); with the whole round 20.7 ms (21-23 ms at 400-609), 2.1M (max 3.0M); draw calls ~1.8k in every run; sector 6 Pearl (final) 19.7 ms, 0 dot clouds (round one: 373), 465 Pearl records on average on hubs 0, 1, 2, 7 and 11, 1583 hand-overs, no shader error in the console

node: test/surface-hubs.mjs (twelve hubs, every point within 0.65 rad, a hub's plane turned onto the sphere to 1e-6 m, the remap, the hysteresis, the attributes within sixteen; a body handed to another hub keeps its origin, anchor and drawn pearl within 5 cm, its hop going on; the seam puts an antipode record on hub 1 and hands it hub to hub to the heart); test/body-reach.mjs (freeReach bisected to step/16, the fixed grid, the cell walk equal to brute force from anywhere, the query over a graph corridor; every Pearl tier for a minute of hops in a synthetic corridor toward targets in the rock: no stalk, cup or anchor on a blocked cell, 220-750 m made along it); test/pearl-impact.mjs (the stagger: snapped, knocked along and aside, squashed 0.55 and rebounding below zero, then the deflate; the recoil; the jolt about its size, sharper for a cored body, a crowd of forty rams under the clamp and under 2.5 single kicks); test/cutis-maku-swarm.mjs (culling: horizon and behind the camera, the levels, the cap, the hysteresis), test/cutis-maku-cores.mjs (the pearl's two resolutions, the depthless twin, the ice), test/pearl-enemies.mjs (dressed everywhere, a full pool refuses, the ice through the seam, the heap, the in-place contact), test/creature-ramp.mjs (the probe's validity); npm test 245 programs, npm run check, npm run build, npm run architecture (td-tab.js 6141 of 6400, no line over 500)

scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --pearl-story: PASS (sector 2's waves all Pearl, 0 undressed; six records at the antipode on hub 1 within 1.6 radii of their records; five audits over ten seconds: 0 of ~210 stalks or anchors across a BLOCKED cell, 0-2 bodies standing on the rock; a rammed amoeba held in its stagger, knocked 2.9 m, the hull's kicks counted; a touched rolling mine recoiling alive; a slowed drifter iced and thawed; no shader error); --creature-probe (the eight Cutis and Reed tiers, the card's pending and refused, dying and pending per step): PASS; --boss-cutis: PASS after the hubs' attribute fix (the first cut failed it: "Too many attributes (iHub)")

not verified: a headed look at the stagger and the hull's jolt in play (headless runs the presentation through the same calls the enemy loop makes, not a tank driven onto a body); a headed close look at stalks against a wall (the audit and a headless close look only); the stalks' sideways sweep while seeking and the membrane itself are not constrained by the rock; the high hull's cap of 12 a tier was not exercised in the soaks (no body that close)
